chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Farsi, from Suleiman ibn Hafs Al-Basri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The guest is treated with kindness for two nights. So when it is the third night, he is from the people of the household; he eats what he finds.'
ai.seo_question: How long should a host provide full hospitality to a guest according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the baseline for *karam* (generosity) by distinguishing between the obligatory hospitality for the first two nights and the voluntary, familial inclusion on the third. Scholarly commentary notes that this transition reflects the shift from a guest's right to a brother's status, emphasizing that the host should treat the guest with the same ease and lack of formality as a member of the *Ahl al-Bayt*. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on social cohesion and the spiritual merit of integrating strangers into the domestic sphere.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Hassan Bin Al Husayn Al Farsy, from Suleyman Bin Hafs Al Basry, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The guest would be kind with for two nights. So when it is the third night, so he is from the people of the household. He eats what he comes to’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Hassan ibn af-Husayn al-Farsi from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Basriy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “Special treatment should be offered to a guest for the two nights; but in the third night he is of the people of the family, and he eats what he receives.’””
